units.translation: as in Eur. Med. 964 δύστανε μοίρας ὅσον παροίχει [wretched one, how much of your fate has passed by]. The scholiast noted καὶ τοῦτο ποιῶν ἐκτὸς ἔσομαι τοῦ νείκους θεοῖς ὑπηρετῶν [and by doing this I shall be outside the quarrel, serving the gods], from which Paleius wrote ἢ κάρτα νείκους τοῦτο δρῶν παροίχομαι [or in doing this I am far beyond the quarrel], with the words θεοῖς ὑπηρετῶν [serving the gods], which are a gloss on the words τοῦτο δρῶν [doing this], written separately. Thus Turnebus
The toil is past, and for the dead it is past, never again to care about rising up.
